hook: Calling someone nice used to be an insult.
modernAnchor: A kind word, a good meal, a pleasant afternoon. We call it nice.
journey: Latin nescius meant not knowing, built from ne, not, and scire, to know. It described someone who simply did not know.
Old French took it as nice and gave it an edge: foolish, simple, slow.
English borrowed that insult in the 1200s, then spent four centuries sanding it down. Foolish became fussy, fussy became precise, precise became delicate.
Delicate slid into agreeable, and the word that once called you stupid turned into the mildest compliment in the language.
